title: Geographic Information Systems
award: Certificate of Achievement requiring 16S/24Q to fewer than 30S/45Q units

program.section_heading: Certificate of Achievement Geographic Information Systems
outcomes: Demonstrate an understanding of what a GIS is, how it can be used, and how the technology has come to be.
Explain, in detail, the nature of geospatial data and associated systems – types, formats, structures, models, acquisition, maintenance, manipulation, and display.

Apply critical thinking skills to the approach of establishing a basic GIS and using said GIS to analyze pertinent data and information to derive results that can or may help to better understand a perceived real-world geospatial phenomenon.
Use the latest, basic GIS-based software technologies on the market with effective and efficient application.

Be academically prepared to obtain an entry-level position directly in GIS, or to greatly supplement and enhance another chosen career field that can benefit from the technical nature of GIS knowledge.
careers: GIS Technician for private entity or government agency

blocks.name: Certificate of Achievement Geographic Information Systems

notes: The stated certificate total (16 units) is also recorded as the block's stated total; the listed course units sum to 16.

The second Career Options line ('Supplemental GIS education to add to existing or future education in another field...') describes a use of the certificate, not a career, so it was not recorded as a career. The Program Highlights section also mentions an 'entry-level GIS Technician'; this was treated as the same career as the one listed.
